why: Window with a frequency map: an anagram of p is any length-|p| window with the same letter counts. Slide a fixed window of size |p| over s, updating 26 counts as one letter enters and one leaves, and record the start whenever the counts equal p's.
hints: Sorting every window is O(n * m log m). What fixed-size summary of a window decides whether it is an anagram of p?
Its letter counts. When the window slides by one, only two counts change: the entering letter +1, the leaving letter -1.
Keep count arrays for p and for the window (or one difference array and a counter of mismatched letters). Compare after each slide; record start = i - m + 1 on a match. O(26 n) or O(n).
pitfalls: If p is longer than s, there are no answers.
Windows overlap, so one letter can belong to several matches.
constraints:
• 1 ≤ s.length, p.length ≤ 3 × 104
  • s and p contain only lowercase English letters
  • (Standard bounds for this exercise; the source gives none.)
